cards.q: Find the first index with `a[i] >= x` in a sorted array.
cards.a: `x` larger than every element, where the answer is `a.size()` and `a[mid]` must not be read there; a run of equal values, where stopping at the first hit returns a middle copy; `lo + hi` overflowing on ranges near `INT_MAX`.

cards.q: Binary search on the answer for the smallest feasible value.
cards.a: A lower bound below a hard minimum, such as a capacity under the heaviest item, because the feasibility check may still pass; no feasible value at all, which needs a separate check; overflow in `mid` or in the running total inside the check.

cards.q: Search a rotated sorted array.
cards.a: Two elements left, where `lo == mid` requires `a[lo] <= a[mid]`; duplicates such as `{1, 0, 1, 1, 1}`, where `a[lo] == a[mid] == a[hi]` hides the sorted side and forces a linear shrink.

cards.q: Find all unique triplets that sum to zero.
cards.a: Anchor dedupe against `a[i + 1]`, which loses `{-1, -1, 2}`, so compare with `a[i - 1]`; all zeros such as `{0, 0, 0, 0}`, which must give one triplet; repeats on the inner pointers after a match; `int` overflow when values approach the limits.

cards.q: Sort an array of 0s, 1s and 2s in one pass with three pointers.
cards.a: A value swapped in from `hi` is unseen, so `i` must stay put; stopping at `i < hi`, which leaves the last element unchecked in `{1, 0}`; an unsigned `hi` wrapping below 0 on an all-2s array.

cards.q: Find the longest substring without repeated characters.
cards.a: `abba`, where a last-seen index behind the window moves the left edge backwards unless you take `max`; updating `best` only on a repeat, which misses a window that reaches the end, as in `abc`; characters outside `a-z` when counting in an array of 26.

cards.q: Find the minimum window of `s` containing all of `t`.
cards.a: Repeated characters in `t`, where `aa` needs two copies, so a set is not enough; no valid window, which must not return `INT_MAX` or a leftover substring; measuring the window after the shrink instead of before it.

cards.q: Find the longest subarray with sum at most `k` using a sliding window.
cards.a: Negative values, where adding an element can lower the sum, so shrinking is invalid and you need prefix sums; `k < 0` with non-negative values, where `while (sum > k)` runs `lo` past `hi` and off the array.

cards.q: Count subarrays with sum `k`.
cards.a: Subarrays starting at index 0, which need the map seeded with `{0: 1}`; negative values and zeros, which rule out a sliding window; `k = 0`, where inserting the current prefix before the lookup counts an empty subarray; prefix overflow in `int`.

cards.q: Count subarrays with sum divisible by `k`.
cards.a: Negative prefixes, because `%` keeps the sign in C++ and -1 must become `k - 1`; the seed for remainder 0; a prefix that is never reduced, which can overflow `int`.

cards.q: Find the next greater element in a circular array.
cards.a: One pass misses answers that wrap around, so scan `2n` positions with `i % n`; equal values, where `<=` treats a tie as greater; an all-equal array, which must give -1 everywhere.

cards.q: Find the largest rectangle in a histogram with a stack.
cards.a: Increasing heights, where bars stay on the stack unless a final 0 sentinel flushes them; an empty stack after a pop, where the width is `i`, not `i - top - 1`; area overflow in `int` for large heights.

cards.q: Remove the `n`-th node from the end of a list.
cards.a: `n` equal to the length, which removes the head and needs a dummy; a one-node list, where the result is null; looping until `fast` is null instead of `fast->next`, which leaves `slow` on the target rather than before it.

cards.q: Reverse a sublist between positions `m` and `n`.
cards.a: `m = 1`, where the head changes, so start from a dummy; not linking the old first node to the node after `n`, which cuts the list; `n` at the tail, where that next node is null.

cards.q: Find the node where a list's cycle begins.
cards.a: No cycle, so test both `fast` and `fast->next` before stepping; testing `slow == fast` before the first move, which is true at once; starting `fast` one step ahead, which breaks the reset-to-head distance argument.

cards.q: Validate a binary search tree.
cards.a: A deep node that breaks an ancestor's bound while passing its parent's check; node values equal to `INT_MIN` or `INT_MAX`, which need `long long` or null bounds; duplicates, which strict comparisons must reject.

cards.q: Find the maximum path sum in a binary tree.
cards.a: All-negative trees, where the answer is the largest node and not 0; clamping a child's gain at 0 while still counting the node itself; returning a forked path to the parent, which may extend only one side.

cards.q: Find the lowest common ancestor in a binary tree.
cards.a: One target being an ancestor of the other, which the recursion must return at once; a target missing from the tree, which the usual version still reports as found; repeated values, so compare pointers instead of values.

cards.q: Serialize and deserialize a binary tree.
cards.a: Missing null markers, which lose the shape; negative or multi-digit values, which break character-by-character parsing; a read index passed by value, which repeats tokens.

cards.q: Find a BFS shortest path in a grid.
cards.a: Marking cells at pop, which queues them repeatedly and can blow up time and memory; start equal to target, which must return 0; a blocked start or target; swapped `m` and `n` on non-square grids.

cards.q: Run Dijkstra's algorithm with a heap.
cards.a: Marking a node done when first relaxed instead of when popped; stale heap entries, which need `if (d > dist[u]) continue;` before expanding or counting; `int` distances overflowing on long paths; negative edges, which the algorithm cannot handle.

cards.q: Run a topological sort with Kahn's algorithm.
cards.a: A cycle, where the output is shorter than `n` and that must be checked; repeated edges when adjacency is a set but indegree counts every copy; nodes that appear in no edge, which are lost if the node list is built from the edges.

cards.q: Flood fill a region with a new color.
cards.a: New color equal to the old color, where the recolor no longer marks cells and the recursion never ends; reading `g[r][c]` before the bounds check; recursion depth on a large uniform grid.

cards.q: Implement union-find with a component count.
cards.a: Uniting two elements already in one set, which must not decrement the count; linking elements instead of their roots; reading `p[i]` instead of `find(i)` at the end; deep recursion in `find` without union by size.

cards.q: Solve 0/1 knapsack on a one-dimensional table.
cards.a: An upward capacity loop, which reuses an item; `dp` filled with 0 when the weight must be met exactly, which needs a negative sentinel with `dp[0] = 0`; value totals overflowing `int`.

cards.q: Find the fewest coins that make an amount.
cards.a: Unreachable states at `INT_MAX`, where `+ 1` overflows to a negative count; amount 0, which must return 0; coins larger than the amount, which give a negative index; greedy choice, which fails on `{1, 3, 4}` for amount 6.

cards.q: Find the longest increasing subsequence with binary search.
cards.a: Equal values, where `upper_bound` allows ties and strict increase needs `lower_bound`; reading `tails` as the subsequence, which it is not.

cards.q: Count the ways to decode a digit string with `1 = A` through `26 = Z`.
cards.a: A leading `0`, which gives 0 ways; `10` and `20`, where the 0 only works with the digit before it; `30` or `00`, which make the whole answer 0; `27`, which is only one way.

cards.q: Find the maximum product subarray.
cards.a: A negative value swaps the largest and smallest products, so track both; updating `lo` from the already updated `hi`; a 0, which resets the run; a single negative element, which is its own answer.

cards.q: Parse a signed integer from a string.
cards.a: `-2147483648`, which overflows if you build the positive value in `int`; overflow that must be caught before `res * 10`; a sign with no digits after it; leading spaces and a stop at the first non-digit.

cards.q: Reverse the digits of an integer.
cards.a: A reversed value above `INT_MAX`, such as from `1534236469`; `abs(INT_MIN)`, which overflows; negative values, where `%` gives a negative digit; trailing zeros, which must vanish.

cards.q: Split a string on a delimiter.
cards.a: `substr(pos, n)` takes a length, not an end index; `find` returning `npos` for the last token; consecutive or trailing delimiters, which produce empty tokens.

cards.q: Merge overlapping intervals.
cards.a: A contained interval such as `[1, 10], [2, 3]`, where the end must be the `max` of both; unsorted input; touching intervals `[1, 2], [2, 3]`, which need a decision on `<` or `<=`.

cards.q: Find the minimum number of meeting rooms.
cards.a: A meeting that ends exactly when another starts, where ends must sort before starts for half-open times; comparing a new meeting with the last one added instead of the earliest end; input not sorted by start in the heap version.

cards.q: Rotate an array right by `k` steps.
cards.a: `k >= n`, which needs `k %= n`; an empty array, where `k %= n` divides by zero.

cards.q: Compute `x` to the power `n` by squaring.
cards.a: `n = INT_MIN`, where `-n` overflows, so widen to `long long`; `n = 0`, which gives 1 even for `x = 0`; under a modulus, the product of two residues overflowing `int`.

cards.q: Print a matrix in spiral order.
cards.a: A single remaining row or column, which the backward passes visit twice without `top <= bot` and `left <= right` checks; non-square matrices; an empty matrix with `g[0].size()`.

cards.q: Implement an LRU cache.
cards.a: `put` on an existing key, which must update and refresh without evicting; popping the list before reading the key to erase from the map; `get`, which must also refresh recency; capacity 1.

cards.q: Implement a stack with constant-time minimum.
cards.a: Repeated minimums, so the min stack must push on `<=`, or popping one copy loses the others; `pop` or `top` on an empty stack; differences overflowing `int` in the single-stack trick.

cards.q: Find two indices that sum to a target with a hash map.
cards.a: An element paired with itself, so look up before inserting; repeated values such as `{3, 3}`; a stored index 0 read through `operator[]` as false.

cards.q: Sort with a custom comparator.
cards.a: `<=` or `>=`, which break strict weak ordering and make `sort` undefined; ties that need a secondary key, since `sort` is not stable; a comparator written as `a - b < 0`, which can overflow.

cards.q: Count set bits by shifting an integer.
cards.a: Negative input, where `>>` on a signed value keeps the sign, so `while (x)` never ends and you need `unsigned`; `1 << 31`, which is negative as an `int`; `1 << 40`, which is undefined and needs `1LL`.
